$comment: Path -> Playwright spec map for the CI e2e selector. Read by scripts/e2e-selection.ts. FAIL CLOSED: a changed file that matches neither always_full, a feature rule, nor skip_e2e forces a full e2e run. Adding a spec without wiring it here fails scripts/e2e-selection.test.ts. Precedence per file is always_full -> features -> skip_e2e -> full.
always_full: $comment: the Playwright setup and its helpers; a change here changes how every spec runs
$comment: build and module graph; one changed line can change how every spec is bundled
$comment: web entry, shared chrome and shared primitives; every screen renders through these

$comment: the vault gate wraps every screen — RequireSession renders it before any route — and its useVaultStatus drives the legacy plaintext startup too, so a changed line can change how any spec boots. Not a vault-only feature rule (#231)
$comment: components imported by more than one page (catalog by items/sale/purchase, parties by parties/party-detail/sale/purchase); a rule would under-select, so they are critical

$comment: pages that render an already-critical shared component tree (components/catalog/** by items/sale/purchase, components/parties/** by parties/party-detail/sale/purchase), plus stock.tsx which items.tsx imports as StockForm. Those components are driven by specs from more than one feature rule, so the page's own rule kept under-selecting; round 3 widened the three known rows first and then promoted the page so an unknown reach costs a full run, never coverage (#231). A promoted page's specs stay reachable through its unit-test sibling in the feature rule.
$comment: the API is one router over one store; a changed line can move any screen, so no per-module rule is claimed
$comment: the wire contract is read by every screen
skip_e2e: $comment: no browser surface; checks and rust still run
$comment: unit tests and their harness never reach the browser; a feature rule above still wins for the test files it names

features.$comment: catalog + stock: item, category and stock screens; stock.tsx and items.tsx are always_full, so the remaining match selects their specs for the unit-test files and the still-mapped categories.tsx (#231)

sale checkout, and the write-window/learnability invariants that exercise it. sale.tsx is always_full (it renders the shared catalog + parties pickers); items-flow.spec.ts drives the sale zero-price quick-add and customer-name-variants.spec.ts the party-picker warning, so both are named here for the unit-test sibling and in case the page is ever un-promoted (#231)

purchase intake, plus the learnability.spec.ts cases that pin the purchase form and its pinned bar at the two short window heights the owner uses (#231). purchase.tsx is always_full (shared pickers + InvoiceHeader); the rule keeps the specs reachable for the unit-test sibling
invoice list/detail, the shared invoice header (which the purchase page also renders) and the new-return form (ReturnsPanel), which returns.spec.ts drives through the invoice page (#231)
the printable receipt document and the invoice print route
the returns flow and its voucher document

customers + suppliers list and detail pages; parties.tsx and party-detail.tsx are always_full (shared components/parties tree), so this rule keeps the specs reachable for the unit-test files. phone-identity.spec.ts is the #129 party-phone rule and rpc-helpers.spec.ts drives actAndAck over customersCreate, so both ride this page (#209 drift)
supplier-adjustment.spec.ts drives the supplier-credit label and total on /debts (lines 162-167), so a debts.tsx-only diff must run it (#231)
profit report and the expense history that feeds it
backups.spec.ts drives the activity table's backup-filename render (lines 39-42), so an activity.tsx-only diff must run it (#231)
settings, theme/preferences, and the vault unlock surface
the dashboard carries onboarding and the low-stock view
auth is the one API area with dedicated specs; the rest of apps/api is critical
